Rafiq-ul-Huque, Senior Advocate with Abdur Razzaq, Senior Advocate with Mohammad Hossain, Ehsan Siddique, Advocates—For the Petitioner.

full_judgment:
3. The complainant opposite party made a petition of complaint on 6-4-2003, which gave rise to Petition Case No. 956 of 2003 impleading the accused petitioner as accused No. 3 described him as Chairman, Siddique Textiles (Weaving) Ltd along with 6 others of them Siddique Textiles (Weaving) Ltd is accused No. 1 and is represented by Managing Director of the Company, alleging therein the complainant is a payee and holder of a cheque given to him by Engineer AFM Siddique being the Managing Director of accused No.1. The cheque was issued on 6-3-2003. It has further been alleged that the complainant had a business transaction with Mr Siddique and his company namely, Siddique Textiles (Weaving) Ltd and Sodtex Ltd over the years for which he (accused No.2) took a loan from him, amounting to Taka 1,50,000,00 in writing, on which, the present Managing Director accused No.2, signed as witness. It has further been alleged, out of the outstanding claims, he gave the complainant some cash on different dates and also issued 5 different cheques amounting to Taka 75,00,000 in 1998 and the cheques were returned to him as unpaid and the complainant contacted him (accused No. 2) but he expressed his regret and apology with an assurance of paying his claim, stating that, due to financial hardship of the company, he needed some time. It has been stated thereafter on good faith and good relationship the complainant did not proceed with the said dishonoured cheques. Thereafter, it has further been alleged, that, in the last part of December, 2002 the said Managing Director of the Company issued four post dated cheques in favour of the complainant being; 

 of First Security Bank Ltd Dilkusha Branch, Dhaka. It has been alleged that these four cheques amounting to Taka 1,00,00,00 were issued to the complainant out of his claims which are partial payments of outstanding claims to the company. The complainant submitted one cheque in the Bank which is subject matter of this case Le. cheque bearing No. FSB/CD 0114045 dated 6-3-2003, on 5-3-2003 in his Bank Account. The said cheque was forwarded to the concerned Bank for encashment on 6-3-2003 but the said cheque was returned to the depositing bank, that is, Uttara Bank Ltd Bangha Bandhu Avenue Branch, as unpaid with an endorsement "Balance Insufficient". The complainant immediately contacted the present Managing Director of the Company, accused No. 2. It has further been alleged that the cheque was issued by AFM Siddique as the Managing Director of accused No.1. It has further been alleged that the issuing authority of the cheque is the company for which the company and its directors shall be liable severally and individually if they do not encash the cheque; the Company is still in existence, so, the claim and legal proceeding pursuant to the dishonour of the cheque is against the issuing authority of the cheque, that is, accused Nos. 1 to 7. According to the complainant, since the cheque was not honoured by its Directors, the cheque was issued by the company as being represented by its Managing Director and since the cheque was not honoured by its Directors, who are responsible for the Company, all of them shall be liable for the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, shortly the Act. The petition of complaint further disclosed the facts that the complainant issued notice on all the accuseds on 12-3-2003 within 15 days of dishonouring of the cheque as per provision of section 138 of the Act, which was duly received by all the accuseds on 13-3-2003 but in spite of that, the accuseds did not make any arrangement for encashing the cheque and thereafter, the complainant filed Petition of Complaint describing the cause of action, according to the complaint, arisen on 29-3-2003. 

 5. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12676 of 2003 similar facts were disclosed and the cause of action was described that the complainant came to know about dishonour of the cheque on 7-6-2003 and thereafter issued notice on 8-6-2003 by registered post with acknowledgement due which were received by the accuseds on 21-6-2003 and after expiry of 15 days, the case was filed on 3-8-2003. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12677 of 2003 similar facts were disclosed and the cause of action was described that the cheque was dishonoured on 6-5-2003 and thereafter the complainant issued notice on 14-5-2003 by registered post with acknowledgement due which were received by all the accused persons on 19-5-2003 and the case was filed on 16-6-2003. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12678 of 2003 the cause of action has been described that the cheque was dishonoured on 6-4-2003 and thereafter notice was issued on 17-4-2003 which was received by all the accused persons on 214-2003 and the case was filed on 11-5-2003. 

 6. Mr Rafiq-ul-Haque, learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioner. submits there being no specific allegation against the petitioner that he was in-charge of and responsible to the Company for the conduct of its business at the material time when the offence is alleged to have been committed by the said Company, which is a statutory requirement under section 140 of the Act, and, as such, no allegation has been made out against the accused petitioner under section 138 of the said Act, hence, the continuation of the proceeding is an abuse of the process of the Court and liable to be quashed. In support of his submission, learned Advocate refers to the decisions reported in AIR 1971(SC) 2162, Company Case Vol. 67 1990-1, AIR-1981 (SC)-872, III (2002) Banking Case 600, 11 (2002) BC 523, 1 (2002) BC 725, I (2001) BC (SC)-243, I (1998) BC 435, II (1998) BC 130, 11 (1998) BC 614, 1(1994) BC Mad. 648. 

 8. We have heard the learned Advocates at length and perused the Rule petition along with annexures. We find from the description for initiating the proceeding by the complainant is otherwise good, that is, on the bounce of the cheques the case was filed after giving notice to the accused including the accused petitioner within the period of limitation as described in the Act. The only point make out by the accused petitioner is that as per section 140(1) of the Act, the proceeding against him is an abuse of the process of law and Court and also harassment to the accused petitioner. Section 140(1) of the Act read as; 

 "The Company is still in existence. So, the claim and legal proceeding pursuant to the dishonour of the cheque are against the issuing authority of the cheque, i.e. Accused Nos. 1-7." The accused petitioner is accused No.3. Excepting this solitary statement, that too, without mentioning the name, there is actually no allegation made in the petition of complaint against the petitioner. There is absolutely no allegation against the accused petitioner that he was responsible or in-charge or in contact of the business of the company. The gist of the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the complainant opposite party is, if allegations disclosed implicating the accused, whether there are sufficient materials or not, the proceeding cannot be quashed. We may now refer to the decisions of this Court referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party. In the case of 1994 BLD (AD) 161 it was held that once it is found there is a prima facie case for going to the trial, a criminal proceeding cannot be quashed. On page 178 of the same volume of the Appellate Division the same proposition of law has been propounded that in a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the High 'Court Division cannot embark upon an enquiry to ascertain the truth or otherwise of the prosecution case or of facts which are not in the prosecution case. In the decision reported in 34 DLR (AD) 287, 28 DLR (AD) 38, 38 DLR 18 the same proposition of law has been propounded. The prime question is, there must be a prima facie case which is to be disclosed. In the instant case, we find, the entire allegations of the complaint are disclosed against co-accuseds, save and except solitary statement mentioned hereinbefore, where in without naming or giving any specific description of the accused petitioner, it has been mentioned that accused Nos. 1 to 7 are responsible for dishonouring the cheques. In the entire body of the complaint petition there is not a single word as Chairman, the accused petitioner at any point of time, took part in taking any resolution or decision or had involvement in day-to-day affairs of the Company or in respect of the cheque issued, he took any active part. We find the accused petitioner is one of the three brothers and one sister and he being eldest, was given Chairmanship of the Company for name's sake. Coming to the question whether the applicant as Chairman can prima facie be made an accused because of outstanding liability against the accused company, it is necessary to look into section 140 of the Act. It reads as under: 

 (b) the drawer of a cheque by drawing it, engages that in the case of dishonour by the drawee he will compensate the holder: 

 (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice, in writing to the drawer of the cheque within fifteen days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; and 

 (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or; as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice. 

 (a) no Court shall take cognisance of any offence punishable under section 138 except upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of the cheque; 

 13. Section 30 deals with civil liability in case of dishonouring of a cheque and the same provides that the drawer had to compensate the holder of the cheque. The Legislature has inserted sections 138 and 141, to make out the dishonouring of a cheque to be an offence if the same is dishonoured for want of funds and after service of notice, the amount is not paid within the period prescribed. The offence that is deemed to have been committed under the provisions of section 138 shall be a complete offence only if the three conditions specified in the provisos to the section also exist. 

 14. Mr Rafiqul-Haque, learned Advocate, refers to the decisions reported in AIR 1958 (SC) and AIR 1971(SC) where in we find in a case of Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 it has been held that in a company, person in-charge, who is in overall control of the day-to-day business of the company or firm, is to be held responsible for dishonouring the cheque. Section 23C of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 is verbatim same as section 140 of the Act. It is just a photo of section 140 of the Act. For better appreciation, we may quote section 23C of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947: 

 In the case of AIR 1971 SC what happened was that accused petitioner was convicted upto the Supreme Court. Thereafter, the accused petitioner met the learned Advocate and disclosed to him when the cheque was issued, he was abroad and produced copy of the passport, then a review petition was filed before the Supreme Court of India, and it was held when the cheque was issued, the accused petitioner at the relevant time was not in the country and was not in day-to-day affairs of the company and he cannot be an accused for a cheque which was dishonoured. Several decisions of the Indian Jurisdiction were considered amongst them 62 All LJ 625 is one of the decisions wherein it was held— 

 "There can be directors who merely lay down the policy and are not concerned with the day-to-day working of the Company. Consequently, the mere fact that the accused person is a partner or director of the Company shall not make him criminally liable for the offence committed by the Company unless the other ingredients are established which make him criminally liable." Decision reported in AIR 1981 SC 872 relied by the learned Advocate for the petitioner is a case under Drugs and Cosmetics Act. We find section 34 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act is the same as section 140 of the Act, which we may quote for better appreciation: 

 In that case also it was held that a person who is not in overall control of the day-to-day business of the company or firm cannot be held responsible for any misappropriation done by the company. It has further been held that unless the complaint does not disclose any participation of the accused in the business of the firm under the partnership deed, the accused petitioner cannot be liable for any mischief of the company. In the decisions reported in Companies Case Vol. 67 (1990) 1 the same proposition of law has been propounded that unless it has been disclosed that partner was responsible for carrying on the business and all the partners were in the conduct of the business of the firm, nonparticipating partner cannot be held responsible for the offence by the company. This case was on Haryana Rice Procurement (Levy) Order, 1979. In the decision of II (1998) Banking Cases 614 cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner it has been held that; 

 "From an analysis of the judicial opinion, what emerges is that every director of the company is not automatically vicariously liable for the offence committed by the company. Only such Director or Directors who were in charge and responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company at the material time when the offence was committed by the company alone shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. It is not as if every Director and the Board of Directors can be said to be responsible to the Company for the conduct of its business. It is not as if every director participates in day-to-day management of the affairs of the company. It is needless to reiterate that only such Directors who were in charge and were responsible for the conduct of the company's business alone shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence under section 138 of the Act. The person in charge and responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company need not be a Director. He can be an officer of the company or a Manager or the Secretary as the case may be. But he is authorised to be in charge for the conduct of the business of the company. The persons responsible for the conduct of the business and in charge of the business of the company need not necessarily be a Director. Therefore, what is required for holding a person vicariously liable for the offence committed by a company is the actual role played by such person in the management and conduct of the business of the company. All such persons who are responsible in the management of the business of the company and in charge of its business at the material time when the offence was committed by the company shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence." 

 16. We find in the entire body of the complaint no assertion has been made that the accused petitioner at the relevant time was responsible or was in day-to-day affairs or was in know of or taking part in issuing the cheque on behalf of the Company. Keeping the decisions of the aforesaid citations, the law and the allegations made against the accused petitioner, which we have quoted earlier, we find the accused petitioner make out a case within section 140(1) of the Act and if this proceeding is allowed to continue against him that will not give any fruitful result to the complainant and that will perpetuate an injustice to the accused petitioner which will defeat ends of justice, and to secure ends of justice, we are of the view this proceeding against the accused petitioner being an abuse of process of law and fact, we have no other alternative but to quash the proceeding against the accused petitioner. We find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner. 

 In the result, all these Rules are made absolute. The proceeding of Petition Case No. 956 of 2003, Petition Case No. 2314 of 2003, Petition Case No. 1736 of 2003 and Petition Case No. 1333 of 2003 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka so far as it relates to the accused petitioner AKM Siddique, Chairman, Siddique Textiles (Weaving) Limited is quashed.
